subject: Clarify downstream ownership and telemetry consent for MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Susan Keller <susan.keller@nimblehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimblehealth.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form redlines — ownership, training, telemetry

Diego — attaching our redline of the MSA and the proposed Order Form. We have three principal asks we need aligned before procurement can move forward: 

1) Output ownership: NimbleHealth needs downstream productization rights for outputs generated by your service when those outputs are solely derived from NimbleHealth inputs (prompts, uploaded data). We found Redwood's current language to be too broad — can you confirm whether you will assign customer title or grant an exclusive right for those outputs?

2) Training/data use: We require explicit opt-out language for training on customer data, with a clear mechanism (API flag and contractual restriction). If Redwood intends to use any customer-provided data to improve models, we need to understand scope, retention, and whether we get attribution/evidence.

3) Telemetry & telemetry retention: We ask for limitations on telemetry retention and an audit trail for request/response pairs used for telemetry analysis. Additionally, we want a limited feedback license so that any feedback submitted to your support/feedback channels cannot be used to train models without our consent.

Please see the attached redline for inline comments. We are aiming for procurement sign-off by the end of next week (3/24). Can you confirm what concessions Redwood can make and whether you can provide a proposed redline for our team to review?

Thanks,
Susan Keller
Senior Counsel, NimbleHealth
Susan.Keller@nimblehealth.com

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — ownership, training, telemetry

Susan — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Looping in Laura (legal), Ben (revenue ops) and Jordan (product) to propose concrete language and the operational path. Quick notes from me: 

- We are supportive of giving customers strong downstream rights for outputs that are exclusively derived from customer inputs (we typically grant broad usage rights).
- Training opt-out is feasible operationally (API flag + order form exhibit) but it does change model-improvement economics; we usually offer two routes: a strict opt-out (no use for training) or a managed telemetry/aggregate-only program. The strict opt-out tends to come with a modest price uplift or the requirement to use a dedicated/private deployment.
- Telemetry retention and auditability: we can provide retention limits and an evidence package for a procurement checklist.

Laura — can you propose specific contract language to close the three asks? Ben — once we have language, can you prepare an order form path (pricing delta, procurement checklist, DocuSign flow)? Jordan — please note any technical constraints or deployment options that make opt-out cheaper or mandatory.

Happy to hop on a short call if that helps. 

Best,
Diego
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Susan Keller <susan.keller@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form redlines — ownership, training, telemetry

Susan / team — thanks for the clear redline. I reviewed NimbleHealth's edits and propose the following approach to balance Nimble's asks and Redwood's product/econ model: 

1) Output ownership: proposed contract language in Exhibit A (attached) that grants NimbleHealth an exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to use and commercialize Outputs that are both (a) generated by Redwood in response to NimbleHealth-provided inputs and (b) not derived from Redwood pre-existing proprietary model content or third-party licensed content. This preserves Redwood's ability to publish model improvements while giving the customer productization rights for their content-derived outputs. 

Proposed short clause: "Customer shall have an exclusive license to use, reproduce, and commercialize Outputs that are solely and directly generated from Customer Inputs. Redwood reserves the right to use anonymized, aggregated signals for model improvement, subject to the Training Opt-Out below."

2) Training/data use: add an explicit opt-out checkbox in the Order Form exhibit. If customer selects Opt-Out, Redwood will not use Customer Inputs or Outputs for training or model improvement. Opt-Out will be available as a standard option for Hosted API with a 20% usage price uplift, or provided at no uplift if customer purchases Redwood Dedicated or Private with a signed addendum (since dedicated/private deployments isolate data).

3) Telemetry & feedback license: limit telemetry retention by default to 30 days for identifiable request/response logs, with the option to extend for troubleshooting. Provide an auditable evidence package listing timestamps, request IDs, and the mechanism used to scrub PII. For feedback submitted via support channels, propose a narrow non-exclusive, royalty-free feedback license limited to improving support processes only; any use for model training will require explicit opt-in.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Diego/Ben: confirm pricing delta for Opt-Out on Hosted API (Ben: please model a 20% uplift and confirm procurement language).
- Jordan: confirm that telemetry retention 30 days + exportable audit logs are operationally feasible and whether we can offer a 90-day tier for enterprise customers.
- Susan: if this approach is acceptable in principle I will provide a marked-up redline back in track changes by COB Thursday 3/18 so your procurement can internalize.

Attachment: Redwood_proposed_redline_20270317.docx (docx, 92KB)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
